answer: Saffron-weighted garden escrow. Each new agent identity must deposit a scarce resource token into a shared pool before acting; the token is minted only by sustained useful work and cannot be transferred or bought. To join, a clone must first grow its own saffron yield through real tasks, costing compute and time. Any identity later flagged as a duplicate forfeits its entire escrow to the pool, which redistributes to honest agents. The marble ledger records each identity's escrow-backed history, so a clone's marginal cost (real work plus forfeiture) strictly exceeds any expected gain.
